sources.title: Gap retrieval development lectures
textPages: Static scoping determines variable bindings from lexical nesting in the source code. A reference resolves in the enclosing source-code blocks, regardless of the calling sequence.
Dynamic scoping determines variable bindings from the active calling sequence. A reference searches the current activation and then callers for a matching binding.
Lexical analysis groups input characters into tokens such as identifiers, keywords and operators. It supplies a token stream to the parser.
Parsing organizes a token stream according to a grammar and builds a syntax tree. It checks grammatical structure rather than grouping characters into tokens.
A process is an executing program with its own virtual address space and operating-system resources. Isolation separates the address spaces of different processes.
A thread is an execution path within a process. Threads in the same process share its address space and resources, while each thread has its own stack and execution state.
A semaphore maintains a count of available permits. Waiting acquires a permit or blocks; signaling releases a permit. A counting semaphore can allow multiple concurrent entrants.
A mutex provides mutual exclusion for a critical section. One owner holds the mutex at a time; the owner releases it after leaving the critical section.

An observational pilot found a three-point score increase among participants. The difference was not statistically significant. The pilot does not establish causation or a long-term retention benefit.
The fictional Luma sample has seven chambers. This is the original classroom handout and gives no temperature measurements.
Correction to the Luma chamber-count handout: the earlier seven-chamber statement is incorrect. Luma has nine chambers. This correction replaces only the chamber count.
A cache stores copies of data to reduce repeated access cost. A cache hit finds the requested data; a cache miss requires fetching it from the underlying store.
Static typing checks types before program execution. A type checker uses declarations and program structure to detect incompatible operations.
Dynamic typing checks types during execution. Values have types, and an incompatible operation can produce a runtime type error.
Lexical scope and static scope name the same binding discipline in this lecture. Static scope follows source-code nesting and is independent of the active call stack.
A deadlock is a state where tasks wait indefinitely for resources held by one another. Mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption and circular wait are necessary conditions in the standard model.
